business_scope.primary_industry_name: Specialized Air/Sea Transport of Regulated Hazardous Chemicals

DTA Luxembourg-United Kingdom of 24 May 1967, as amended by Protocol of 29 December 2011
DTA Luxembourg-Germany of 23 August 1990, as amended by Protocol of 11 December 2009
DTA Luxembourg-France of 1 April 1958, as amended
DTA Luxembourg-People's Republic of China of 12 March 1983, as amended by Protocol of 21 November 1994
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent BEPS (MLI), signed by Luxembourg on 7 June 2017, effective 1 August 2019
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), Articles 49 and 63 on freedom of establishment and free movement of capital

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML/CFT and UBO legal framework: (i) Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; (ii) Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 27 January 2024 on the Single Register of Beneficial Owners (registre unique des bénéficiaires effectifs); (iii) CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; (iv) Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 January 2019 defining the filing modalities of the RBE; (v) Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, including beneficial-owner declaration and RBE coordination provisions; (vi) Law of 2 September 2011 on the freedom of establishment and the conduct of regulated business activities (applicable to the freight-forwarding authorisation d'établissement).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif de société à responsabilité limitée) and Articles of Association (statuts)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public admitted in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, authorised by the Ministry of Justice
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentic Luxembourg notarial act with statutory legalisation of signatures; an authenticated copy (expédition) is lodged with the RCS by the notary - no apostille required for domestic notarial acts

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity card of each future shareholder, gérant (manager) and every UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Civil registry, passport authority or consulate of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille certificate for documents from the 125 Apostille Convention states; Consular Legalization through a Luxembourg embassy/consulate for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Clean criminal record extract (extrait du casier judiciaire) or equivalent certificate of no convictions for each gérant and, if applicable, authorised director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent criminal records authority of the country of residence (e.g. ministry of justice, police or judicial registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn translation into French, German or Luxembourgish; for EU member states the Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 multilingual certificate waiver may apply

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Banker's capital subscription and deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des souscriptions) evidencing the SARL share capital before the notarial deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg credit institution or EU credit institution branch established in Luxembourg (e.g. BIL, BGL BNP Paribas, ING Luxembourg) regulated by the CSSF and the Law of 5 April 1993
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank attestation addressed directly to the notary; no apostille required for documents issued by a Luxembourg-authorised credit institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn translation (traduction assermentée) of each document not drafted in French, German or Luxembourgish
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court-appointed sworn translator registered with the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified translation appended to the notarial deed; the translator's signature is legalised by the notary - no apostille applied to the translation itself

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of all shareholders, UBOs, gérants and key counterparties against the EU consolidated financial sanctions lists (Council Regulation (EC) No 2580/2001, (EU) No 881/2002, Council Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and No 833/2014 as amended), the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, the OFAC SDN List for all USD-denominated wire traffic and SWIFT flows, the Luxembourg national freezing list administered by the Ministry of Finance, and the FATF public statements and EU AML high-risk third-country list. Politically exposed person (PEP) status must be determined in accordance with FATF Recommendation 12, Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD 5) and CSSF Circular 17/650, covering foreign and domestic PEPs, family members and close associates. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandatory for the DG/hazmat forwarding structure (banking_aml_risk_tier: High_Risk_Special_License), including source-of-wealth documentation, independent bank reference, adverse-media screening and UBO natural-person verification at the 25% threshold.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) - official portal https://www.lbr.lu and RESA electronic publications portal https://www.resa.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names are admissible in the three administrative languages of Luxembourg (French, German, Luxembourgish) using Latin script; any foreign-language denomination must be accompanied in the Articles of Association by a French/German/Luxembourgish rendering or description of the business purpose; transliteration from non-Latin alphabets (Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic) is rejected unless an officially certified transcription is filed with the RCS and the original script is reproduced in the notarial deed; the legal-form token 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée', 'S.à r.l.' or 'SARL' is mandatory and must appear in identical form in all commercial correspondence and invoices. Names must be distinctive, truthful, not misleading and not identical or confusingly similar to any existing RCS-registered name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Crédit / Établissement de crédit - requires prior CSSF authorisation under the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector
Insurance / Assurance / Réassurance / Courtage en assurances - requires prior authorisation of the Commissariat aux Assurances (CAA)
Fiduciary / Fiduciaire / Trust / Fiducie - requires the Luxembourg professional licence for fiduciary services (PSF) under CSSF regulation
SICAV / SICAF / FIS / Investment Fund / Fonds d'investissement - requires prior CSSF investment-fund authorisation
Exchange / Bourse / Securities / Titrisation - requires a CSSF broker-dealer or market-operator licence
État / Grand-Duché / National / Royal / Communal / Ministère - implies public authority and requires a Grand-Ducal decree of prior authorisation
Union Européenne / EU / European / Euro - when used in an official or misleading connotation requires prior ministerial approval
Société Anonyme / SA / SCA / SECA - alternative legal-form tokens incompatible with the SARL designation and therefore prohibited in the statistical name
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon an RCS refusal notice (refus d'inscription) pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies, the following procedure applies: (1) informal cure - the notary resubmits a modified corporate name within five working days, with a supplementary statement of distinctiveness; (2) formal administrative appeal (recours hiérarchique) to the Director of the Luxembourg Business Registers within one month of notification, attaching the statutory grounds, the proposed name and the preliminary search report; (3) if dismissed, an annulment action (recours en annulation) lies before the Tribunal administratif de Luxembourg within three months of the notification of the refusal (per amended Law of 21 June 1999, Article 11), with further appeal available to the Cour administrative; a stay of execution may be requested urgently (référé suspension); estimated filing costs EUR 85 per instance. Alternatively, the applicant may file a completely new name application at the RCS, which is processed within five business days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for the ISIC 5229 DG/hazmat forwarding licence. A virtual office or letterbox arrangement is structurally rejected by the RCS, the Ministry of Mobility and Public Works (transport directorate) and the CSSF for anti-abuse purposes (Law of 10 August 1915 as amended, and the CJEU letterbox-company jurisprudence, C-191/15 X TBG). The DG forwarding SARL must maintain from day one a physical principal establishment (siège réel) in Luxembourg - leased or owned office space, an appointed local gérant with decision-making authority, an operational ADR safety adviser (conseiller à la sécurité), local insurance and liability cover, and tangible records of transport-origin documents. Commercial substance requirements are elevated because the target payment rails (SWIFT wire, letter of credit) and the Dangerous Goods sector are classified as High_Risk_Special_License under the national AML methodology.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary name search and negative certificate (certificat négatif de nom) through the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)/RCS database
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary public (disbursement to LBR computerised search)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff scale - fixed search and certificate fee, EUR 150-250

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation notarial deed: drafting of Articles of Association (statuts), S.à r.l. constitutional formalities, subscription and deposit of share capital, appointment of gérant and first accounting reference date
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (Grand-Ducal Regulation of 17 February 1976, ad valorem/deed basis); prevailing market benchmark EUR 3,500-5,000 for a standard SARL with non-resident shareholders

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS initial filing fee for the deposit of the constitution (dépôt de la société au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory schedule of fees under the Law of 19 December 2002, approximately EUR 270

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RESA legal publicity insertion (publication obligatoire au Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice / Luxembourg Business Registers (RESA service)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory flat publication tariff, approximately EUR 160

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RBE (Single Register of Beneficial Owners) initial filing - UBO identification, confirmation of 25% ownership/control threshold and consent documentation pack
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (the register filing itself is free) plus law firm professional handling fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for regulated professional filing and UBO piercing analysis

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalisation of foreign passports, UBO identity documents and criminal-record extracts of future gérants
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent issuing authority of the foreign state and Luxembourg consular/embassy services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document Hague Apostille fee and consular legalisation tariff, EUR 25-85 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation fees (traduction assermentée) for non-French/German/Luxembourgish documents into French or German, as required by the notary and the RCS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-approved sworn translator registered with the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate EUR 40-80 per page plus certification certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Autorisation d'établissement (business licence) application for freight forwarding and transport arrangement activities under the Law of 2 September 2011
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministère de l'Économie / Direction générale des classes moyennes (Luxembourg Ministry of Economy)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing tax approximately EUR 75-300 depending on branch of activity, plus professional handling fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-filing of the special DG/hazmat licence for ISIC 5229 regulated chemicals forwarding - ADR, IATA DGR and IMDG compliance statement, safety case and transport authorisation dossier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministère de la Mobilité et des Travaux publics (Ministry of Mobility and Public Works, transport directorate) and external DGSA/safety consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for dangerous-goods licence advisory and compliance assessment; statutory administrative fees are minor

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Appointment and pre-incorporation verification of the ADR Safety Adviser (conseiller à la sécurité / qualified person for dangerous goods), including mandate, certificate check and organisational reporting lines
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External certified ADR safety adviser service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market annual retainer benchmark EUR 900-1,800, pro-rated for the pre-incorporation and initial operational phase

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 180 to 187-24 (SARL regime); Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and annual accounts, Article 11 (RCS registration); Law of 2 September 2011 on access to crafts, small business and the exercise of liberal professions (establishment permit)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 9 bis rue Emile Lavandier, L-1401 Luxembourg, electronic filing portal e-RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Authentic notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) including the articles of association (statuts), executed before a Luxembourg notary and e-filed with the RCS via the e-RCS platform
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed capital EUR 12,000; 100% of shares must be subscribed; at least 20% (EUR 2,400) must be paid up in cash at incorporation into a blocked escrow account (compte de consignation) held with a Luxembourg credit institution; in-kind contributions must be fully vested before notarial execution
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned founder-members, acting for the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) in formation, resolve: 1. The subscribed share capital of EUR 12,000 is allocated to the founders as stated in the notarial deed, and the blocked deposit is approved as paid-up portion. 2. The registered office is fixed at [Registered Address], Luxembourg. 3. [Name of Gérant] is appointed sole Gérant (managing director), empowered to represent the Company and to sign all filings. 4. The Gérant is authorised to complete RCS, tax, VAT, EORI, social security, establishment-permit and customs registrations. 5. The opening of corporate bank accounts is ratified and payable mandates granted. Adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Check and Pre-Incorporation Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS index search online and notarial pre-verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an RCS index search and national trademark register search to confirm name availability and absence of third-party conflicts; verify that the corporate object matches ISIC 5229 specialized DG forwarding; instruct the notary to prepare the draft articles of association (statuts) with registered office and management clauses.
required_dossiers: Draft corporate object (DG freight forwarding, ISIC 5229)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File an alternative name immediately; narrow the corporate purpose wording; supply corrected founder identification within 24 hours to avoid re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Account and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) authorized to hold escrow accounts for companies in formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the SARL in formation; deposit at least EUR 2,400 (20% of minimum capital EUR 12,000) or the full subscribed amount; obtain a bank certificate of blockage (attestation de blocage) addressed to the notary evidencing the paid-up cash contribution; complete KYC/AML declarations including ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) details.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of founders and managers
KYC/AML forms and declaration of beneficial owner
Confirmation of DNFP (Déclaration sur l'honneur) for ADR/DG activity scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the high-risk DG profile, provide the draft freight forwarding license, DG safety adviser (DGSA) appointment and ADR compliance procedures; alternatively select another Luxembourg credit institution and re-issue the blockage certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Deed of Incorporation and Statuts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before a Luxembourg notary with all founders; the notary verifies the blockage certificate, identity documents and legal capacity; the deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) is executed, founding members subscribe the capital, initial gérant(s) are appointed, and the registered office is declared; the notary forwards the file electronically to the RCS.
required_dossiers: Original passports and birth certificates of founders and managers
Criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) of each manager
Lease agreement or address authorization for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Execute an acte rectificatif to correct any error in the deed; provide missing exhibits (address lease, police certificate) before the RCS filing deadline; reschedule notarial execution on the next business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Publication in the Official Electronic Gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary e-files the notarial deed, statuts and annexes through the e-RCS platform; the RCS verifies the formal legal requirements and registers the company with a legal personality; the registration abstract is published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA); an RCS extract (extrait) is issued to certify legal existence.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation (original, electronically transmitted)
Declaration of subscription and payment of capital
Acceptance letter of the appointed gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any RCS request for regularization within 15 days; file an amending notarial deed to align the statuts with RCS instructions; resubmit clean certified documents via the notary; escalate through the e-RCS helpdesk in case of portal errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration: Corporate Income Tax, VAT and EORI Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and Administration des contributions directes (ACD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the corporate income tax and municipal business tax registration (form 1 / módèle TVA) with the ACD; file the VAT registration application with the AEDT; apply for an EORI number for customs declarations concerning cross-border DG freight; elect the place of supply for freight services under Article 44 of the VAT Directive, when applicable.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of gérant(s) and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is queried, provide certified French/German translations and clarify the cross-border DG forwarding service scope; send a formal request via registered letter to the AEDT/ACD director; appeal to the administrative authority if registration is refused.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Security Registration with the CCSS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register as a social security employer with the CCSS within 8 days of hiring any first employee; obtain the employer and employee registration numbers; register the gérant(s) under the applicable social security scheme using the Guichet.lu e-administration platform.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of gérant(s) and future employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct missing affiliation data online through the CCSS exchange portal; re-send the registration forms via Guichet.lu; contact the CCSS back office to cure identification mismatches.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Establishment Permit and Dangerous Goods Freight Forwarding License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for SMEs (Direction générale des classes moyennes), in coordination with the Ministry of Mobility and Public Works – Transport Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the middle-class establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011 for freight forwarding; in parallel, apply for the freight forwarder license (licence de commissionnaire de transport) under the Law of 5 April 1993; provide proof of professional competence and good conduct; appoint and notify a Dangerous Goods Safety Adviser (DGSA) under ADR Chapter 1.8, and file the DGSA certificate with the Transport Administration.
required_dossiers: Criminal record extract (good conduct) of the natural-person manager or legal entity representative
Proof of managerial or professional competence (diploma or 3-year experience in transport/logistics)
DGSA certificate (ADR 1.8.3) and notification of appointment
Financial capacity declaration (own funds and liability insurance)
DG freight forwarding liability insurance certificate covering hazardous cargo
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused, file a letter of reconsideration (recours gracieux) with the Minister of the Economy within 3 months; after confirmation, appeal to the Administrative Tribunal (tribunal administratif) within the same deadline; supplement the file with additional proof of DG professional competence or ADR training certificates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Permit (Commodo/EIA) and Civil Defense Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Environnement (Environmental Agency) and Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a commodo environmental authorization application under the Law of 15 June 2018 for the DG warehouse and transshipment facility; prepare a hazard analysis of chemical storage and a fire safety concept; if the stored quantities of dangerous goods exceed Annex I/II thresholds, apply for a full environmental impact assessment under the Law of 15 May 2018; obtain structural load certification and coordinate with CGDIS for fire safety inspection.
required_dossiers: Site plan and structural load certificate from an approved engineering office
Hazardous chemicals inventory and safety data sheets (SDS)
Fire safety concept and CGDIS fire certificate
Commodo opinion or full EIA report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Complement the application upon written request of the Environmental Agency; participate in the public consultation or hearing; after refusal, lodge a letter of reconsideration and thereafter an appeal to the Administrative Tribunal within 3 months of the negative decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for SMEs (Direction générale des classes moyennes), jointly with the Ministry of Mobility and Public Works – Department of Transports (Administration des transports)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Commercial Establishment Permit, Law of 2 September 2011) / Licence de commissionnaire de transport (Freight Forwarding License, Law of 5 April 1993) / Dangerous Goods Safety Adviser (DGSA) Notification under ADR 1.8.3

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environmental Agency), Ministry of Environment, Climate and Biodiversity, 1 avenue du Rock'n'Roll, L-4361 Esch-sur-Alzette
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 1A – Environmental Authorization (Commodo) under the Law of 15 June 2018; a full Environmental Impact Assessment under the Law of 15 May 2018 is triggered when DG storage/transshipment exceeds Annex I/II thresholds, including any Seveso lower-tier or upper-tier hazardous quantities; otherwise a registration/commodo opinion applies
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater effluent: COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, TSS ≤ 35 mg/L per the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 29 May 2019 on effluent discharge; VOC emissions ≤ 20 mg C/Nm³ in waste gases (Directive 2010/75/EU - IED as transposed by the Law of 15 June 2018); secondary spillage containment and drainage isolation per ADR 1.4; hazardous waste dispatches only through licensed operators per the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste management

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) after technical inspection covering fire resistance of the DG warehouse, sprinkler/suppression systems, segregation of incompatible substances and emergency egress; structural load inspection certificate from an approved engineering office verifying racking and floor load capacity for hazardous goods; workplace clearance from the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail et des Mines - ITM) confirming appointment of the DGSA, provision of personal protective equipment, and first-aid readiness

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA – AEDT) for VAT; Direct Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes – ACD) for corporate income tax; single digital portal: MyGuichet.lu and guichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity that is not established in Luxembourg but makes taxable supplies of dangerous-goods forwarding services must obtain a Luxembourg VAT number (numéro de TVA) from AEDT via the 'Demande en vue d'obtenir un numéro d'immatriculation TVA' (Form 710). The application must indicate a Luxembourg tax representative if the entity has no permanent establishment and no fixed establishment. Supporting documents include notarized/chamber-certified certificate of incorporation, statute, board resolution appointing the representative, a completed NACE/ISIC classification (5229 corroborating DG forwarding), and evidence of the cross-border transaction structure. For a resident SARL, the RCS (Luxembourg Business Registers) matricule number serves as the national tax ID; the ACD assigns a corporate tax file number on incorporation. The VAT number is issued in the format LU12345678 and conferred immediately upon registration; approval generally takes 5–15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Luxembourg-resident SARL is subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (CIT) on worldwide profits; branch/PE of a non-resident is taxed on Luxembourg-source income; no territorial exemption or tax-exempt zone applies. For VAT, the SARL is a taxable person under Article 4 of the VAT Law; the DG forwarding activity is an established business in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime is available. Luxembourg permits a group VAT registration (unification de la TVA) under Article 61 of the VAT Law, allowing related taxable persons to file as a single VAT person. For direct tax, a resident SARL may elect fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) with a qualified Luxembourg parent under Article 164bis LIR for CIT/NAM. Hybrid Mismatch Elections: taxpayers must document and disclose hybrid mismatch arrangements under ATAD (Articles 60bis–60quater LIR); no elective exemption is permitted, but a 'reverse hybrid' treatment is automatically applied when the entity is treated as transparent in its U.S./foreign jurisdiction and the SARL is an EU resident company — note that Luxembourg is not a check-the-box jurisdiction, and entity classification for U.S. Federal purposes follows treasury regulations, not Luxembourg election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA) governed by the Luxembourg Law of 12 February 1979 on VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 for non-resident suppliers that have a fixed establishment or that supply services subject to Luxembourg VAT at the place of supply; Luxembourg-established small businesses with annual turnover (excluding VAT) of EUR 30,000 or less qualify for the small-business exemption under Article 57 of the VAT Law and may be exempted from VAT registration. The DG forwarding contract value will almost always exceed this, and for dangerous-goods services VAT registration is mandatory irrespective of threshold because the customer is usually a taxable person with the place of supply in Luxembourg or another EU Member State.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose real-time electronic fiscal clearance, digital stamping, QR-code coding, or a continuous API-based clearance/reporting system for B2B VAT. Electronic invoicing is standard and legally valid under Article 14 of the VAT Law; invoices may be issued via PEPPOL, EDI, or signed PDF. For B2G (public-sector contracts), electronic invoicing via the national Peppol infrastructure is mandatory for invoices over EUR 3,000 (Grand-Ducal Regulation). Taxpayers must retain a SAF-T (Standard Audit File for Tax) export capability upon AEDT request; there is a statutory requirement to preserve invoices in original form (XML/PDF/EDI) and to grant access to fiscal auditors. In practice, DG freight contracts should include invoice lines with 0% VAT codes and the customer's EU VAT ID to substantiate intra-Community treatment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported outside the EU are zero-rated under Article 42 of the VAT Law (exportation), provided the goods physically leave the EU and the exporter retains evidence of departure. Freight, packing, insurance, or forwarding services directly linked to exported goods are zero-rated under Article 46. Intra-Community dispatches to a taxable person in another EU Member State are exempt under Article 43 only if the supplier records the customer's validated EU VAT ID and the goods are transported to that state. For DG/Hazmat forwarding, the zero-rating defence requires a consignment-specific dangerous goods declaration (DGD) and transport document proving actual cross-border movement; if the service relates to goods stored or consumed in Luxembourg, Luxembourg VAT at 17% applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD – Single Administrative Document) filed via the EU Export System (ICS/ECS) including MRN; for dangerous goods, also the consolidated dangerous goods declaration and IMDG/IATA documentation.
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document showing physical exit from the EU; for DG freight this must include UN numbers, Class labels, and proper shipping name.

Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 / Letter of Credit evidence of payment received from the foreign buyer in convertible currency (where applicable; Luxembourg does not impose FX controls, but banks require underlying transaction documents).
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or untrue zero-rating declarations trigger mandatory VAT repayment to the State plus default interest of 0.8% per month (or part thereof) from the VAT due date, administrative fines up to EUR 2,500 or, in serious cases, 10% of the evaded VAT under Article 211 of the VAT Law; if goods do not leave EU within the documented period, the zero-rating is retroactively cancelled and a 17% VAT assessment issued. Under the Customs Law (Code des douanes), false declarations are punishable by confiscation of goods, fines up to three times the evaded duties, and criminal penalties for smuggling; AEDT retains a five-year limitation period for assessments, extendable to ten years in cases of fraud or omission. For DG freight, document retention of at least ten years is mandatory for explosion and environmental safety records under national transport legislation, and the tax audit will reconcile the DG manifest with export declarations and freight receipts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking supervision and the European Central Bank (ECB) for monetary policy and euro-system legal framework
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a eurozone member and applies the full EU Treaty principle of free movement of capital. There are no exchange controls, no convertibility restrictions, and no prior authorisation for current or capital account transactions. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, and liquidation proceeds may be freely transferred in EUR or any foreign currency, subject solely to standard corporate law formalities (annual account approval, distributable reserves) and to the reporting obligations under BCL Balance of Payments statistics. The domestic law, primarily the Luxembourg Law of 5 September 2016 on the free movement of persons and capital, confirms the absence of any administrative transfeison limitation. In practice, funds are converted via commercial banks with standard anti-money laundering (AML) checks, but there is no reliance on central bank approvals or perpetual exchange control hurdles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender rules exist in Luxembourg or under EU law. Luxembourg does not require exporters to repatriate trade receivables within a specific timeline, nor to convert receivables into euro or any other currency. For statistical purposes, payments for exports of goods exceeding a certain threshold form part of the BCL's quarterly balance of payments data collection and must be reported by resident banks or, in certain circumstances, by the resident enterprise under the Grand-Ducal Decree of 23 October 2002 relating to external trade statistics. However, these reporting obligations do not create mandatory conversion ratios, holding period limits, or surrender duties. A dangerous-goods forwarder may therefore maintain cash flows in original invoicing currency and execute spot conversions only when operationally required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with dedicated trade finance and LC desk
Operational Account and Foreign Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low-to-Medium for a Luxembourg-domiciled SARL active in hazardous goods forwarding. Luxembourg recognises authorised electronic money institutions (EMIs) supervised by the CSSF, as well as EU/EEA EMIs passporting under PSD2. Such institutions can be used narrowly for client this reason. For payments, however, major Luxembourg clearing and settlement infrastructure. For operational disbursements and receipt of trade proceeds, banks provide a broader range of clearing rails. The core impediment is not electronic money licensing per se but the high-risk classification of the ISIC 5229 / dangerous goods model, which multiply the obligational scrutiny of the EMI's own correspondent banking network. Most non-bank payment institutions terminate or heavily restrict onboarding because of the perceived sanctions and trade-based money laundering exposure. The use of an offshore digital EMI (outside EU / EEA) is generally commercially impractical because no Luxembourg private equity or lending counterparty will accept a non-bank offshore account as the primary treasury vehicle for statutory capital, LC issuance, or supplier guarantees, constraining liquidity and clearing efficiency.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg banks and funds organisations do not impose a universal statutory requirement for directors to appear physically before the account-opening bank. However, in practice, for high-risk clients such as a dangerous-goods freight forwarding company, face-to-face identification of at least one signatory director and senior compliance officer is expected. Remote onboarding is only granted if the corporate bank has deployed a qualified video-identification solution certified under Luxembourg Grand-Ducal Regulation (e.g., Ganassi identification by eIDAS-compliant qualified signature). The ultimate beneficial owners, directors, and any authorised signatories must nonetheless provide an original or notarially certified copy of passports, proof of address, and recent official extract from the Luxembourg Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS). For specifically
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.High_Risk_Special_License: A minimum of one executive director and, absent unusual engagement, the chief financial officer or treasury manager responsible for banking signatures will be asked to attend an interview at bank premises or via BCL-compliant video procedure, supported by AML/KYC presentation of the business plan, target counterparties, and internal red flag controls for hazardous goods shipping.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector blocking due to ISIC 5229 and non-corporate DG automobile of Hazmat chemicals where the bank's radiance surfaces the sanctions list, terrorism financing risk, dual-use goods, or unforeseen TMT exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate dossier containing the SARL's RCS extract, certified statutory audited financial statements or opening balance sheet, valid CargoX forwarders license and regulatory permits (e.g., ADR / IATA DG permits), list of Qualified Economic Operators under the Union Customs Code (AEO status), or each banking counterparty, standard transport contracts, key client list, third-party transport and subcontractor Due Diligence Policies, a comprehensive written AML/KYC manual, sanctions screening procedure, and a written narrative of the transaction flow detailing how shipping and forwarding fees are isolated from cargo costs and how ecart payments or counter, so as to demonstrate that accounts are not used to settle underlying third-party goods trades or provide unlicensed financing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction red flags: involuntarily involving ultimate beneficial owners or clients resident in san, a jurisdiction subject to FATF or Luxembourg high-risk list, where transactions habitually settle through offshore accounts or wire corridors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A UBO-box disclosure including a copy of holding structure and chain of title, beneficial owner passports / residence certificates, random financial base share to the source of wealth, bank reference letters, sworn tax residency certificates, an intensive governance package with an external compliance advisor review, trade counterparty onboarding dossier including licence verification, certificate of good standing for all customers and counterparties, and an independent business-risk assessment with a documented mitigation matrix confirming no shipments to sanctioned entities or military end-users.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and trade-based money laundering flag originating from freight invoices, custom declarations, or dangerous goods paperwork that contain inconsistent description, valuation mismatches, or triangulated routing through high-transshipment hubs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete transaction-following file with commercial invoices, packing lists, B/L or airway bill, and CMR/ADR waybills, linked to a historical transaction archive covering 24 months, a written Trade Compliance agreement with the bank allowing sampling audits, a transaction monitoring dashboard with real-time filtering against EU / UN / US OFAC / UK HMT consolidated sanctions lists, a Thomas the Tank and IT security framework, evidence of employee anti-bribery training, and an independent review letter from a customs broker confirming commodity classification, quantities, valuation, and end-user certificates for all regulated dangerous goods.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital is normally routed through SWIFT MT103 payments denominated in EUR or major currencies from the counterparty bank to a Luxembourg credit institution where the SARL maintains an opening account. The reference must include an unambiguous sender-to-receiver or beneficiary reference matching the capital contribution and the entity's commercial unique code. For statutory equity injection, the bank applies the BCL Individual Balance of Payments (BoP) category code 7021 for direct investment equity, while remuneration for operational prepayments or inbound prepayments of freight charges are attributed to codes under trade in services (e.g., 619 for transport services). Verification protocol combines SWIFT network tracing, sender / receiver name matching, and a segregated inward debit advices used by the statutory auditor to certify the capital under the Luxembourg law. For crypto assets or funds routed via shadow clearing or stablecoin bridges, no credible Luxembourg bank will accept the inbound as proper capital or trade settlement; these are categorically rejected on AML grounds. All inbound flows must come from a bank account held in the name of the investor or customer and cannot be aggregated or remitted from opaque intermediary holding accounts without a full explanation and evidence of the underlying relationship. Inward funds subject to foreign exchange conversion must be matched against a proactive tenor-limit spot or forward in a designated corporate dealing account and cannot be placed through a spread-only fintech engine without a valid client-pass documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements by the Luxembourg SARL will be executed through commercial bank clearing rails. Preferable for settlement with ocean / air carriers, customs authorities, and sub-contractors is the SWIFT MT103 direct correspondent clearing network, using the stated across-border BIC/IBAN. This supports wire transfers in EUR, USD, and other freely convertible currencies. For larger consents covering charters, consolidation, and COA (Contract of Affreightment) payments, or to harmonise delayed settlement conditions with suppliers, the commercial letter of credit (LC) is the principal clearing instrument, issued by the Luxembourg bank in favour of carriers and terminal operators. The bank will apply ICC UCP 600 and eUCP 2.0 rules, and documentation will include AWS and original transport documents. The company must establish separate subsidiary treasury operational policies so that outbound disbursements for freight and handling use reality but exact original invoice mapping; outlay for customs duties is made directly to the customs authority via designated account, never to a third-party broker unless under strong for services. For repetitive high-frequency payouts, the bank offers XML electronic file (pain.001) and the automated reconciliation service through cash management and SWIFTNet services, reducing operational risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain Vanilla FX Forward contracts up to 18 months tenor for hedging transportation revenue and carrier payable currency mismatches (EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, EUR/GBP).

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in limited currencies such as CNY and KRW, permitted only where the underlying freight invoice exposure is demonstrably settled in an inconvertible currency, with confirmation concatenated to the bank dealing room and subject to CSSF and EMIR reporting.

Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) for rolling short-term liquidity and matching of large charter / demurrage cash flows, entered under ISDA / CEMA agreements and subject to clearing and margin thresholds, without speculative intent.

Currency options (European-style) used solely for firm contract bidding in tender situations where there is a high probability of award and an operational requirement to cap foreign currency denominated liabilities, adhering to prudent hedging policy and no proprietary trading mandate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, notes, and management report when required) with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS/LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve annual accounts within 6 months after financial year-end; filing with the RCS must occur within 1 month after approval, in all cases no later than 7 months after the balance-sheet date (e.g., 31 July for a calendar-year SARL).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry notice requiring regularisation within 30 days; court-ordered coercive fines (astreinte) and administrative penalties up to EUR 5,000 (approx. USD 5,460); persistent non-compliance after judicial notice may lead to administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) data in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due every calendar year before 31 March; any change in beneficial ownership, including a shareholding transfer that alters UBO percentages, triggers a separate modification filing within 30 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines for the entity and responsible officers, with Luxembourg penalty ranges up to EUR 40,000; publication of sanctions; repeated default is referred to the Public Prosecutor and may result in enforcement proceedings against the SARL and its managers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return covering corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC), and net wealth tax (IFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December balance-sheet date, the combined annual tax return is due by 31 December of the following tax year (e.g., financial year 2024 due by 31 December 2025); quarterly advance payments are due on 1 February, 1 May, 1 August, and 1 November.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge and statutory default interest at 0.6% per month on outstanding tax; ex-officio assessment by ACD if no return is filed; continued default may trigger enforced collection and liability exposure of the SARL’s managers.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent audit is mandatory where the SARL exceeds at least two of the following three indicators at balance-sheet date: total balance sheet above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average workforce above 50 employees. A statutory audit may also be required as a condition of the dangerous-goods freight forwarding licence or under AML high-risk special-licence conditions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002, as amended, transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); EU-IFRS is permitted for non-listed SARLs and is mandatory for issuers on regulated markets.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must complete the RBE online annual confirmation before 31 March each calendar year, attesting that the disclosed beneficial owner(s) and their percentage of ownership or control are current. Any shareholding transfer that changes the UBO structure must be filed as an RBE modification within 30 days; the annual confirmation is not waived by such an update and must still be performed on or before 31 March.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholders' and managers' meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,000 – 2,800 per year for registered office and corporate agent services in Luxembourg City; higher where independent directorship or substance support is required.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 – 30,000 per year for a full Lux GAAP audit of a small dangerous-goods forwarding SARL, depending on transaction volume and group structure.
